source: High Country Fly Fishing Experts like Due South Outfitters

conditions.overall: Wild streams are fishing well following recent rains — the sweet spot came as water cleared but hadn't fully dropped, and fish are still actively feeding as levels continue to fall. Delayed Harvest season ends June 6, opening those streams to harvest and likely reducing quality quickly.

top_flies.name: Yellow Sally
top_flies.note: Effective dry fly for wild streams during summer; good attractor pattern for High Country freestones

top_flies.name: Sulphur Dry
top_flies.note: Major evening hatch happening in droves on the Watauga tailwater; also productive on wild streams

top_flies.name: Yellow Rubber Leg Stimulator
top_flies.note: High-floating attractor; use as dry in dry-dropper rigs on wild mountain streams

top_flies.name: Yellow Humpy
top_flies.note: Classic High Country attractor dry; pairs well as the top fly in a dry-dropper setup

top_flies.name: Yellow Chernobyl / Chernobyl Ant
top_flies.note: Foam attractor dry for wild streams and tailwaters; high visibility and floats a dropper well

top_flies.name: Frenchie
top_flies.note: Go-to nymph dropper for both wild streams and tailwaters; fish below a dry or under an indicator

top_flies.name: Perdigon
top_flies.note: Fast-sinking nymph; excellent dropper on wild creeks as water levels drop and fish become wary

top_flies.name: Sulphur Nymph
top_flies.note: Match the hatch subsurface on the Watauga and South Holston during sulphur activity

top_flies.name: Blowtorch
top_flies.note: Hot-bead nymph; effective dropper on wild streams, especially in lower clearer water conditions

top_flies.name: Zebra Midge
top_flies.note: Tailwater staple on the Watauga and South Holston; fish near the bottom during generation

top_flies.name: Soft Hackle
top_flies.note: Swing through runs and seams on the tailwaters, especially effective during sulphur hatches

top_flies.name: Baetis Nymph
top_flies.note: Subsurface tailwater pattern; fish along the bottom during high generation flows

tactics: Fish wild streams with a dry-dropper rig — use a larger attractor dry (Yellow Stimulator, Humpy, or Chernobyl) with a small nymph dropper (Frenchie or Perdigon #18-20) to cover both surface and subsurface feeding lanes.
As water levels drop on wild streams, stay well back from the hole you're fishing — low clear water makes trout spooky, and wading too close will blow your opportunity before you cast.
Downsize flies in low, clear conditions — switch to smaller dry flies and nymphs (#18-20) to reduce surface commotion and present a more natural profile to wary fish.

On tailwaters during high generation (Watauga and South Holston), follow the TVA release schedule closely — the first day of low water after generation can produce spectacular fishing, especially with sulphur hatches.
Target evening hours on the Watauga tailwater for sulphur hatches — fish Sulphur Dries #14-18 and Soft Hackles #16-18 during and after the hatch window.
Avoid Delayed Harvest streams starting June 6 — once harvest regulations open, fishing quality drops quickly as pressure increases; seek wild stream alternatives instead.

For wade anglers on the South Holston, monitor TVA generation schedules daily — the river is running all-day generation and wading is currently difficult, but low-water windows can open up prime fishing.

waters.name: Wild Streams — Western North Carolina (High Country)
waters.note: Fishing well post-rain as water has cleared and stabilized. Stay back from pools, downsize flies, and fish dry-dropper rigs. Fish are actively feeding despite dropping levels.

waters.name: Watauga River (Delayed Harvest — Boone/Valle Crucis)
waters.note: Delayed Harvest season ends June 6 — harvest opens Saturday. Expect fishing quality to drop sharply as angling pressure increases. Seek wild stream options after this date. Next stocking in October/November.

waters.name: Watauga River Tailwater (East Tennessee)
waters.note: Running all-day generation — great for drift boat anglers, tough for waders. Sulphur hatches occurring in droves in the evening. Fish Sulphur Dries #14-18 at dusk. Watch TVA schedule for low-water windows.

waters.name: South Holston River Tailwater (East Tennessee)
waters.note: Also running all-day generation. Reports not as strong as the Watauga but fish are still being caught. High water should jump-start the sulphur hatch. Wade anglers should monitor TVA generation schedule and target first-day low-water opportunities.

elevation_note: High Country streams near Boone (3,300-4,000 ft) run 1-2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC — hatches, flows, and seasonal transitions all lag slightly compared to streams at lower elevations.
stocking_note: NC Delayed Harvest streams close to catch-and-release regulations on June 6, 2026 — harvest opens that Saturday and fishing quality typically drops quickly. Next stocking for DH waters is scheduled for October and November. Hatchery Supported streams in Avery County (North Toe River, Elk River, Linville River) were stocked in March and May 2026.
